title: Week of July 27, 2026: PFAS Water Plant, a Woodbury Road Order, and 647 Homes in Lake Elmo
summary:
This week: Lake Elmo advances its PFAS South Water Treatment Plant; Woodbury orders a 2027 street reconstruction and authorizes easement acquisition; a 647-home development comes before the Lake Elmo council; and the county board prepares to spend on courthouse security. Plus a Stillwater water-tower update and the week ahead.

WHAT'S IN THIS EPISODE
- Lake Elmo (Tue July 21): Council approved Task Order #33 with Bolton & Menk for $45,000 to finish preliminary design of the South Water Treatment Plant, the next PFAS-removal plant planned on an 8.2-acre site the city is acquiring; the cost is reimbursable through the 3M settlement grant program. Before the meeting, the council met in closed session to weigh offers to buy two properties (one on 34th St. N.).
- Woodbury (Wed July 22): After a public hearing, the council ordered the 2027 Roadway Reconstruction project (Res. 26-87), hired Bolton & Menk for final design at $374,450, and authorized easement acquisition and, if necessary, condemnation. It also awarded ~$282,505 (Solid Rock, drive-aisle patch/reseal), ~$265,212 (Solid Rock, apparatus-bay roof), and ~$276,255 (Bergerson-Caswell, wells 7 & 16 rehab), and approved a Gold Line maintenance agreement with the Met Council.
- Lake Elmo (Tue July 21): Limerick Village, the city's largest proposed housing development — 647 homes on ~80 acres east of Manning Ave by Maplewood Development — came before the council on its preliminary plat and PUD. A state 120-day deadline of Aug. 5 requires a decision within two weeks.
- Stillwater (Tue July 21): Water-tower repaint change order (J.R. Stelzer, +$8,410, total ~$650,690); Washington Square Park pavers (Schifsky, not to exceed $20,000); extension of the Sheriff's-Office records agreement; and an ordinance making the council's Planning Commission seat nonvoting.

THE WEEK AHEAD (meetings & how to weigh in)
- Washington County Board — Tue July 28, 9:00 a.m., Government Center, 14949 62nd St. N., Stillwater. Agenda: courthouse security upgrades ($434,908.66, Parallel Technologies); ERP software study ($299,300, Plante Moran); a Land & Water Legacy conservation easement on 27 acres in Marine on St. Croix; and a 2027 budget workshop for the county's Community Development Agency. Public comment at the start of the meeting; comment cards to the County Board Clerk. Agenda: washingtoncountymn.gov/AgendaCenter
- Oakdale City Council — Tue July 28, 7:00 p.m. public hearings, 1584 Hadley Ave. N. Agenda: purchase-and-development agreement with Tanners Lake L.L.C.; award of the Willowbrooke Fields restroom/shelter contract (Res. 2026-49) plus ~$99,000 in shade umbrellas; public hearings on a new tobacco license and a secondhand-goods dealer renewal; claims of ~$1,702,657.72. Special workshop Wed July 29. Agenda: oakdalemn.gov/AgendaCenter
- Stillwater-area school board (Stillwater Area Public Schools) — Tue July 28, 5:30 p.m., Oak Park Learning Center, 6355 Osman Ave. N., Stillwater. Student handbook; annual policy reviews (student discipline, public-data requests, crisis management, student technology); first reading of an off-campus-activities policy; closed sessions on a real-property matter and the superintendent's performance review. Up to 15 public speakers, 3 minutes each. Chair Alison Sherman; Supt. Michael Funk. Agenda: meetings.boardbook.org/Public/Organization/2592
- Lake Elmo City Council — next meets Tue Aug. 4 (the Aug. 5 statutory deadline on Limerick Village falls that week). Agendas: lakeelmo.gov/AgendaCenter

SOURCES: Official city, county, and school-district agendas, packets, staff reports, and resolutions — City of Lake Elmo (July 21 regular + special), City of Woodbury (July 22), City of Stillwater (July 21, via Granicus), Washington County (July 28), City of Oakdale (July 28), and Stillwater Area Public Schools (July 28). Full document references are in the build folder.

Produced from a Christian understanding of what matters in public life; it reports the facts and does not tell you what to conclude.
